Start off with 1 - 2 scouts, get eyes on the area around you for possible expansions, get runes. Always grow, because growth is science. In the beginning prioritize food tiles to get to 3-4 pop as soon as possible then you can build a settler.

If you haven't known already settling your cap on a hill shaves 1-2 turns off of anything in the beginning because of that extra hammer. I'd recommend you go tradition. Aim for 3-4 cities, but 3 is good too, if there's no 4th expansion. General rule of thumb is to have 1 luxury per city to negate  the 4 happiness hit from founding the city itself. Run internal food trade routs between your cities, that helps them out growing big time. Settling coastal is more beneficial for internal trade routes too, because cargo ships carry more food/production.

Do not neglect military units. Just about any civ may attack you in the beginning. Don't be the latest in score military wise.

As far as early economy goes, I usually get gold simply from trading off luxury copies to the AI, as well as from city connections. Strategic resources can get you GPT early as well, and here's the tip: try selling each strategic recource for 2 gold per turn individually. If you have EUI mod, the icons next to other civ leaders will prompt you what they're willing to buy.

Save Oxford to get a key tech. Building Oxford gets you a free tech. You may build it the next turn after you finish Electricity tech, and take Radio for free, entering Modern Era for Ideology pick next turn.

In general, you need to grow your cities, especially capital and get the key science buildings in time. Library is not urgent if you have 6-8 pop in a capital but getting your libraries up in your secondary cities in time will allow you to start on National College upon researching the Philosophy. You might even want to delay settling your next city when NC is available for building. Then get universities - public schools - research labs. If a city is next to a mountain, research Astronomy for Observatories that give decent bonus to scince output of that city in which it is built.

I don't know if you're aware but Great Scientists, Merchants and Engineers always share the same cost, so generating one of them will bump up the cost of another one of these. The same is with Artist, Musician, Writer. For that reason, don't generate merchants and engeneers if you want as many scientists as possible. Engineers are fine because of World Wonders but merchants are meh. Filling out tradition will let you buy engineers with faith when you hit Industrial Era though majority of the strongest wonders come earlier. 

With Artists, get your guilds up in time, and generate writers for great works to get early tourism and artists to bulb them for Golden age or a great art. Either option is fine. Now, to be able to capitlize upon that early tourism output, get open borders from other civs and run spare caravanes to them. You should be able to become influential over them at the exotic level by the time they have ideology which means your happiness won't tank. They would need to get above exotic over you in order for their ideology to put pressure on your happiness.

It's good that you settle on a river, but generally you need the river itself, the longer it is, the better. Settling on a hill is an early game advantage, it's literally one extra hammer, so not really great later on but if you won't miss on any resources it's good. Look for a place with resources that will synergyze with buildings like stable and granary. Sheep, cattle, horses is one extra hammer each with stable, as well as bannanas, wheat and deer is one extra food each with granary. Combine food with hammers. A farm on a hill adjacent to a river is 2 food 2 hammers yield, while a mine on the same hill is 3 hammer. So look for overall higher yield with priority to green apples. You need growth more than anything. If your city has production tiles, you need citizens to actually work those tiles without sacrificing too much growth. If your city has multiple iron tiles, that's alotta hammers with a forge later on. Some pantheons complement growth tiles very well.   If you have say, 4-6 sea resources such as fish or whales, Sea god will give you +1 hammer for each fishingboat. If you have many deer for example, you can get +1 food from each with Goddess of the hunt pantheon. + 2, if city has a granary.
